baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.range: Account uses a historical broad species concept
before.summary: An eight-armed cephalopod. The historical common-octopus name covers a species complex; regional identity needs review.

anatomy.name: Eight arms
anatomy.description: Eight retained continuous arm surfaces have selected asymmetric curvature, thick proximal sections, rounded closed ends and moving basal web margins. The head/mantle/crown exterior is joined as a selected field; local arm/web unions remain approximate. A travelling bend and authored proximal elongation illustrate reaching. Mouth/beak, muscles, nerves and physiological control are not reconstructed.

anatomy.name: Suckers
anatomy.description: Selected paired rows with folded external rims, selected radial relief, an uncapped central orifice and short throat. Internal acetabulum/protuberance, microscopic denticles/hairs, pressure, sealing and attachment mechanics are not modelled. Inspection lighting is disclosed separately from natural optical appearance.

anatomy.name: Siphon
anatomy.description: A thin-walled external funnel has an exposed lip and cleared route into a selected illustrative mantle-wall cavity. Cavity shape and tissue connections are unmeasured; valves, respiratory organs, pumping, flow and jet propulsion are not implemented.

behaviors.label: Arm support / extension study
behaviors.description: Finite5.2second authored support/recovery sequence on the same retained arms, webs, sucker exteriors and body. Three selected unevenly timed recovery events advance chosen arms; supported distal target regions compensate for body displacement. Radius/length, contacts and timings are illustrative. No measured recruitment pattern, suction, traction, force balance, full self-collision or complete locomotor simulation.

rendering.reason: External authored arm shapes only; not validated biological locomotion or feeding.

behaviors.label: Exploratory arm reach
behaviors.description: A finite travelling bend and selected proximal extension straighten and lift one anterior arm, followed by return. Radius adjustment illustrates a local area/length relationship, not a validated muscular-hydrostat or strain/force solution. Food contact, prey handling, ingestion and sensing remain absent.

rendering.reason: External authored arm shapes only; not validated biological locomotion or feeding.

behaviors.label: Jet escape — pending
behaviors.description: Jet escape is unavailable: funnel flow, mantle contraction, propulsion and water forces are not implemented.

sources.title: Primary crawling study · Levy, Flash and Hochner (2015)
sources.scope: Selected primary abstract was read from the indexed PubMed/publisher result: non-rhythmic arm recruitment and pushing by elongation. No video trajectories, figures or forces were fitted.

sources.title: Tramacere et al. · Structure and mechanical properties of Octopus vulgaris suckers (2013 online; 2014 issue)
sources.scope: Selected indexed results describe two sucker rows and infundibulum/acetabulum organization; full PMC opening presented a browser check. No actual figure or internal sucker dimensions were obtained. Citation disambiguated using indexed PubMed24284894: online27 November2013, issue6 February2014. The earlier2013 year was not by itself wrong; this is distinct from the PLOS morphology/adhesion paper. Selected indexed morphology/methods were read, not fitted tissue parameters or a new figure inspection.

sources.title: Senckenberg Marinvert · common octopus
sources.scope: Selected indexed adult morphology was read: horizontal pupils, stout arms, double sucker rows, basal web and variable papillose skin. Direct page access returned 401. No foreign-region species-complex determination inferred.

sources.title: Tramacere, Appel, Mazzolai and Gorb (2014) · Hairy suckers
sources.type: Primary morphology study; actual publisher Figure1 and selected methods
sources.scope: Actual publisher Figure1 was inspected: exposed infundibulum, rim and orifice; prepared SEM views distinguish radial/circumferential relief from internal acetabular hairs. Those hairs are not placed on the exposed outer cup. Selected methods describe freshly killed Livorno animals, fixed/dehydrated/coated for SEM; these are not live optical maps. No source pixels, scale fitting or adhesion-force solver is used.

sources.title: Tramacere et al. (2013) · The morphology and adhesion mechanism of Octopus vulgaris suckers
sources.type: Primary morphology and proposed adhesion mechanism; limited access scope
sources.scope: Official seven-page PDF introductory/selected methods text was readable. A figure screenshot request timed out or returned no inspectable image, so no new PLOS figure/video inspection is counted. The internal chamber/protuberance and proposed sealing mechanism are not reconstructed or validated here.

sources.title: Smithsonian Ocean · Octopus shows off its funnel
sources.type: Institutional species/anatomy account; not a collection determination
sources.scope: Actual account text read: the exhalant funnel is associated with the front of the mantle. This supports qualitative anatomical context only; its image was not downloaded and no jetting mechanism or measured pose is inferred.

sources.title: Olga Ernst · Octopus vulgaris, Zoo am Meer (2025)
sources.type: Authentic supplementary captive photograph, CC BY-SA4.0
sources.scope: Actual original1468×906 PNG downloaded and visually inspected whole, author/grant checked at Commons. It shows the mantle opening/funnel under the eye and irregular external tissue. Source caption identification and captive location are retained, not an independent collection determination or wild-range record. Exact unmodified download/delivery checksum and license are in the external-surface report.

sources.title: Hanassy et al.2015 · Stereotypical reaching movements involve bend propagation and elongation
sources.type: Primary kinematic study; actual indexed abstract read
sources.scope: The actual PubMed abstract describes3D reaching reconstructions and variable proximal elongation in nominal Octopus vulgaris. Only selected conceptual mechanisms are illustrated; no trajectories, strain values, fitted forces, full paper figures or video were obtained.

sources.title: Levy and Hochner2017 · Embodied organization of morphology, vision and locomotion
sources.type: Author perspective with selected experimental figures; actual publisher PDF inspected
sources.scope: Actual publisher PDF printedpages3–4 Figure1 andFigure2 were rendered/inspected, with selected text. They show irregular recruitment/contact records and aquarium frames/eye roll in nominal Octopus vulgaris; Figure1 also includes insect comparisons. This is a perspective, not a newly retrieved primary2015 full dataset or fitted control model. No source figures are redistributed.

sources.title: Allen et al.2014 · Comparative morphology of changeable skin papillae
sources.type: Primary comparative morphology; indexed abstract and selected author-hosted PDF text
sources.scope: Selected author-hosted PDF text and indexed abstract were read. A new figure download/render did not succeed. The study distinguishes several cephalopod species and prepared tissue, including nominal O.vulgaris small dorsal/ventral eye papillae from Florida; modern common-octopus-complex identity is not redetermined. No other species compound papillae, measured microanatomy or internal muscles are copied into this surface. Cellular pigment/relief is original numerical artwork guided qualitatively by authentic photographs.

visual.fidelity: Reference-guided authored soft-body reconstruction; unmeasured and partly stylized
visual.scale: normalized display size; not a measurement
visual.description: Eight asymmetrically curved continuous arms now have longer selected arclengths, thicker proximal sections and closed rounded terminal caps. A smoothly joined mantle-wall/head/crown field with integrated eye bulges replaces overlapping lofts. The external funnel has an exposed open route into a selected illustrative cavity. Original cellular pigment/relief stays attached to deforming skin in the main renderer. A finite support/recovery study holds selected distal target regions while the body advances; exploratory reaching combines a travelling bend with selected proximal elongation and radius adjustment. These are authored mechanisms, not measured animal trajectories, pressure/contact solutions or physiological camouflage. Tissue unions, eye and body proportions, papilla distribution and optical response remain approximate.

viewerRig.scope: Unmeasured Qualitative external morphology and finite5.2second nonrepeating authored studies. A closed connected core field includes an illustrative open mantle-wall cavity and a cleared funnel route, not reconstructed internal organs/valves or a water-flow solver. Selected38sucker pairs per arm remain an illustration. Restricted sampled distal interarm clearance checks exclude basal tissue, between-sample and self contacts. Full crawling, suction, prey handling and jetting remain unfinished. Compatibility/export use simpler UV material sampling, with reduced surface fidelity. Source nominal identifications have not been independently redetermined within the common-octopus complex.
